Lists

Working with ordered collections

Creating Lists

List Creation 
// Empty list
ayanmo empty = [];

// Homogeneous list
ayanmo numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5];

// Mixed types
ayanmo mixed = [1, "hello", otito, 3.14];

// Nested lists
ayanmo matrix = [[1, 2], [3, 4], [5, 6]];
// Empty list
let empty = [];

// Homogeneous list
let numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5];

// Mixed types
let mixed = [1, "hello", true, 3.14];

// Nested lists
let matrix = [[1, 2], [3, 4], [5, 6]];

Direct Index Syntax

Access elements directly with bracket notation:

Index Access 
ayanmo fruits = ["apple", "banana", "cherry"];

ayanmo first = fruits[0];    // "apple"
ayanmo last = fruits[2];     // "cherry"

// Modify by index
fruits[1] = "blueberry";
Irosu.fo(fruits);  // ["apple", "blueberry", "cherry"]

Accessing Elements: Ogbe

Use Ogbe.ohun() for access and Ogbe.iye_ohun() for length:

Reading from Lists 
ayanmo fruits = ["apple", "banana", "cherry"];

Ogbe.ohun(fruits, 0);        // "apple"
Ogbe.ohun(fruits, 2);        // "cherry"
Ogbe.iye_ohun(fruits);       // 3
Ogbe.ile(fruits);            // "apple" (first)
Ogbe.oju_ona(fruits);        // "cherry" (last)

// Check membership
Ogbe.ayika(fruits, "banana");  // otito (true)

Manipulating Lists: Ogunda

Use Ogunda for push, pop, and mutations:

List Operations 
ayanmo stack = [1, 2, 3];

Ogunda.fi(stack, 4);        // push -> [1, 2, 3, 4]
Ogunda.fi(stack, 5);        // push -> [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

ayanmo last = Ogunda.mu(stack);  // pop -> 5, stack is [1, 2, 3, 4]

Ogunda.ge(stack, 1);        // get index 1 -> 2
Ogunda.wa(stack, 3);        // contains 3? -> otito
Ogunda.yo(stack, 0);        // remove at index 0 -> stack is [2, 3, 4]

Sorting and Reversing: Ogunda

Sorting 
ayanmo scores = [42, 7, 99, 13, 55];
Ogunda.to(scores);
Irosu.fo(scores);  // [7, 13, 42, 55, 99]

// Reverse in place
Ogunda.pada(scores);
Irosu.fo(scores);  // [99, 55, 42, 13, 7]

Map, Filter, Any, All: Ogunda

Functional Transforms 
ayanmo numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5];

// Map: transform each element
ayanmo doubled = Ogunda.yi_pada(numbers, { x -> x * 2 });
Irosu.fo(doubled);  // [2, 4, 6, 8, 10]

// Filter: keep matching elements
ayanmo evens = Ogunda.yan(numbers, { x -> x % 2 == 0 });
Irosu.fo(evens);  // [2, 4]

// Any: does any element match?
ayanmo has_big = Ogunda.eyikeji(numbers, { x -> x > 4 });
Irosu.fo(has_big);  // otito (true)

// All: do all elements match?
ayanmo all_small = Ogunda.gbogbo(numbers, { x -> x < 10 });
Irosu.fo(all_small);  // otito (true)
let numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5];

// Map: transform each element
let doubled = Ogunda.yi_pada(numbers, { x -> x * 2 });
Irosu.println(doubled);  // [2, 4, 6, 8, 10]

// Filter: keep matching elements
let evens = Ogunda.yan(numbers, { x -> x % 2 == 0 });
Irosu.println(evens);  // [2, 4]

// Any: does any element match?
let has_big = Ogunda.eyikeji(numbers, { x -> x > 4 });
Irosu.println(has_big);  // true

// All: do all elements match?
let all_small = Ogunda.gbogbo(numbers, { x -> x < 10 });
Irosu.println(all_small);  // true

Aggregation: Obara

Use Obara for computing over lists:

Aggregation 
ayanmo values = [10, 20, 30, 40, 50];

Obara.apapo(values);         // sum -> 150
Obara.kere_julo(values);    // min -> 10
Obara.nla_julo(values);     // max -> 50

Iterating Lists

For Loops 
ayanmo cities = ["Ile-Ifẹ", "Ọyọ", "Abeokuta"];

fun city ninu cities {
    Irosu.fo("City: " + city);
}

// Using index with range
fun i ninu range(0, Ogbe.iye_ohun(cities)) {
    Irosu.fo(i + ": " + cities[i]);
}
let cities = ["Ile-Ifẹ", "Ọyọ", "Abeokuta"];

for city in cities {
    Irosu.println("City: " + city);
}

// Using index with range
for i in range(0, Ogbe.iye_ohun(cities)) {
    Irosu.println(i + ": " + cities[i]);
}

What You Learned

  • Creating lists with [] syntax
  • Direct index access and assignment with list[i]
  • Access via Ogbe.ohun(), length via Ogbe.iye_ohun()
  • Mutation via Ogunda.fi/mu/yo
  • Sorting and reversing via Ogunda.to/pada
  • Functional transforms: Ogunda.yi_pada/yan/eyikeji/gbogbo
  • Aggregation via Obara.apapo/kere_julo/nla_julo
  • Iterating with fun/for loops and index access
